purpose: Select a deterministic Comic spring cadence by comparing the foreground silhouette.

reference.image: video-195.jpg from the session frame comparison
reference.alignment: Existing approximate frame-comparison offset; exact audiovisual synchronization was not independently established.

measurement.referenceMask: RGB mask: R > 1.13*G, B > 0.95*R, B > 50; 3x3 maximum filter; largest connected component; interior holes filled. Pixels y >= 350 excluded to separate the attached tube.
measurement.candidateMask: Union of the projected foreground Comic blob triangles at 640x480. Uses the verified object/camera transforms and the full timeline, including spring integration during photo freezes.
measurement.metric: Binary intersection over union (IoU). This measures silhouette agreement; it does not measure material, lighting, texture coordinates, clipping, or pixel-perfect rendering.

conclusion: Retain the canonical 60 Hz spring cadence. Higher cadences substantially worsen this foreground silhouette. The enclosure clipping was separately resolved by restoring the native quarter-scale view transform.

nativeEvidence.nativeGeometryProbe: At the 195.32s timeline state, outer vertex 2611 was replayed through 1997 native spring integrations with the actual elapsed-age history. Its final local coordinates were [-7400.472,6869.155,-5815.036], versus [-7398.916,6870.422,-5813.434] in JavaScript. The raw camera depth is about 15710; native camera preparation scales this by one quarter before clipping and fog, placing it inside the original far limit.

referenceProfile.rationale: All effects use the native view-space clip limits. The earlier extended-far-plane workaround was superseded by the complete native camera-preparation oracle.

caveats: The cadence fit is a single-frame foreground measurement and does not establish the original executable's frame rate throughout the demo.
Reference mask thresholds and the tube exclusion introduce a few pixels of boundary uncertainty.
Native normalization and fixed-point integration produce small deviations from the floating-point spring adaptation.
The reference capture's exact hardware, render cadence, and runtime configuration are unknown.
